Subject: Privacy contract intake - DPA and subprocessors

Hi Priyom,

We’re getting started on the privacy intake for our prospective engagement. Legal asked me to request Redwood's standard DPA and current subprocessors list so we can run initial vendor review and start procurement paperwork. A few specific asks to help us scope: 

- Can you confirm whether Redwood relies on any cloud provider subcontractors that will have access to customer data?
- What transfer mechanisms do you support for EU / UK data (SCCs, adequacy, etc.)?
- Do you have an e-sign preference for execution (DocuSign vs AdobeSign)?
- Any typical redlines Redwood accepts on retention, logging/audit, or audit rights?

If you can send your DPA and subprocessor CSV, we’ll share with our privacy team and give back comments. Target: get this signed before our pilot kickoff (target week of Jan 11).

Thanks — Sam

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the note. Looping in Marissa (Legal) and Laura (Security Ops) to help with the detailed answers. For a quick response: attached is our standard DPA (Redwood_DPA_v1.2.pdf) and the current subprocessor registry (redwood_subprocessors_2026.csv). A few quick points up front: 

- Subcontractors: we use public cloud providers (AWS, GCP) for hosted deployments and a small set of managed infra partners for Dedicated customers. The attached CSV marks their roles and whether they have access to customer content/KV cache.
- Transfers: we support EU-US and UK transfers using the EU SCCs / UK Addendum; we can also discuss transfer impact mitigations if your data residency needs a dedicated region.
- E-sign: we typically use DocuSign, but we will execute via AdobeSign if your legal prefers it.
- Redlines: generally we accept targeted redlines around retention and data subject requests; carve-outs for production telemetry and aggregated usage metrics are typical. For audit requests we provide SOC 2 Type II plus scoped evidence; full on-site audits are handled case-by-case.

Next steps: Marissa will propose a few clarifications and a recommended path for any standard redlines. If you have procurement timelines, please share them and the name/email of your signer.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Priyom — received the DPA and subprocessor registry. A couple quick follow-ups from our privacy team after a first pass: 

1) Would Redwood consider a contractual commitment to notify us of any new subprocessor with 30 days' notice and an objection right? Our default is 30 days; your CSV shows a couple of partners we need to review.
2) We need confirmation that logs supporting audit requests are retained for at least 90 days and can be made available under a standard SOC evidence bundle.
3) On transfers: our counsel prefers the EU SCCs + UK addendum approach; can you confirm you’ll execute those for cross-border processing?

Also, we may push a small set of redlines around the audit clause and indemnity caps — can Marissa/Laura advise what Redwood typically accepts?

One logistical ask: we prefer DocuSign; please send an envelope if that works.

Best — Sam
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Hi Sam —

Appreciate the questions. Quick answers and proposed path: 

- Subprocessor notice: we can commit to a minimum 30-day advance notice for new subprocessors and provide a short objection period. For mission-critical infra changes (e.g., cloud provider upgrades) we may need a faster operational notice, but we will flag material changes in advance. We will include the notice clause in the DPA redline.

- Logs/audit evidence: we retain request/trace logs for 180 days by default; we can provide a SOC 2 evidence packet and scoped logs for audit-related requests. Laura can coordinate the evidence exchange and any secure transfer of artifacts.

- Transfers: Redwood will execute the EU SCCs and UK Addendum for transfers originating in those regions; we'll include the standard execution addendum when we send the envelope.

- Typical redlines: Redwood is open to limited adjustments around retention and audit logistics; we are generally not able to broaden indemnity or exposure materially. For indemnity caps we prefer to keep to the commercial agreement; however, we can accept reasonable tailoring on the audit process and data return/destruction timelines.

DocuSign is fine — we will prepare an envelope that includes the DPA and the SCC addendum and route it to your signer. If Acme requires AdobeSign, note that execution of SCCs sometimes requires specific metadata; please advise if AdobeSign is required.

Next steps I suggest:
- Priyom to confirm signer name and HubSpot deal so we can tie the envelope to procurement (Priyom: please paste HubSpot link).
- Laura will share the SOC 2 summary (SOC2_report_summary.pdf) and coordinate secure evidence transfer.
- I’ll prepare a redline that accepts the 30-day subprocessor notice and clarifies log retention and evidence scope.

Marissa Cole
